steps.body:
\[\frac58-\frac{x+2}{4x}=\frac{5x}{8x}-\frac{2(x+2)}{8x},\qquad x\ne0.\]

Use 8x as a common denominator.
steps.title: Part (a) | Step 1

steps.body:
\[\frac{5x-2(x+2)}{8x}=\frac{5x-2x-4}{8x}=\frac{3x-4}{8x}.\]

Subtract the entire numerator of the second fraction and collect like terms.
steps.title: Part (a) | Step 2

steps.body:
\[(2x-1)(x+4)=2x^2+8x-x-4=2x^2+7x-4.\]

Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second.
steps.title: Part (b) | Step 1

steps.body:
\[3x(2x^2+7x-4)=6x^3+21x^2-12x.\]

Multiply every term by 3x.
steps.title: Part (b) | Step 2

steps.body:
The only possible ordered number pairs are \((1,4)\) and \((2,5)\).

The second number must be exactly 3 more than the first, not merely differ by 3.
steps.title: Solution | Step 1

steps.body:
\[P(1\text{ then }4)=\frac28\times\frac17,\qquad P(2\text{ then }5)=\frac38\times\frac27.\]

There are 7 cards remaining for the second draw; there are two 1s, three 2s, one 4 and two 5s.
steps.title: Solution | Step 2

steps.body:
\[P=\frac{2}{56}+\frac{6}{56}=\frac{8}{56}=\frac17.\]

The two ordered events are mutually exclusive, so add their probabilities.
steps.title: Solution | Step 3

steps.body:
The French-and-German-only region is \(16-x\), and the German-and-Italian-only region is \(15-x\).

The totals 16 and 15 each include the triple intersection x.
steps.title: Part (a) | Step 1

steps.body:
\[6+(16-x)+(15-x)+x=24.\]

The four disjoint regions in the German set must total 24.
steps.title: Part (a) | Step 2

steps.body:
\[37-x=24\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=13.\]

Solve for the common triple-intersection count.
steps.title: Part (a) | Step 3

steps.body:
\[FG\text{ only}=16-13=3,\qquad GI\text{ only}=15-13=2.\]

Use the triple-intersection value from part (a).
steps.title: Part (b) | Step 1

steps.body:
\[F\text{ only}=32-(3+4+13)=12,\qquad I\text{ only}=27-(4+2+13)=8.\]

The French-and-Italian-only count is the given 4.
steps.title: Part (b) | Step 2

steps.body:
\[n(F\cup G\cup I)=12+6+8+3+4+2+13=48.\]

Sum all seven mutually exclusive interior regions.
steps.title: Part (b) | Step 3

steps.body:
\[n(\text{none})=60-48=12.\]

Subtract the union from the total number of students.
steps.title: Part (b) | Step 4

steps.body:
\[\angle ABC=180^\circ-62^\circ-47^\circ=71^\circ.\]

The three triangle angles sum to 180 degrees.
steps.title: Solution | Step 1

steps.body:
\[\frac{AB}{\sin47^\circ}=\frac{13}{\sin62^\circ}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad AB=\frac{13\sin47^\circ}{\sin62^\circ}=10.7680208859\ldots\text{ cm}.\]

Match each side to its opposite angle in the sine rule.
steps.title: Solution | Step 2

steps.body:
\[\text{Area}=\frac12(13)\left(\frac{13\sin47^\circ}{\sin62^\circ}\right)\sin71^\circ=66.1788645053\ldots\text{ cm}^2.\]

Use half the product of two sides times the sine of their included angle; retain unrounded values.
steps.title: Solution | Step 3

steps.body:
\[\text{Area}=66.2\text{ cm}^2\quad\text{(3 significant figures)}.\]

Round only the final area.
steps.title: Solution | Step 4

steps.body:
\[27=3^3,\qquad9=3^2,\qquad\frac{6^x}{2^x}=\left(\frac62\right)^x=3^x.\]

Write both sides in a common base.
steps.title: Solution | Step 1

steps.body:
\[\frac{27^x\times3^{n+6}}{9^{4-n}}=3^{3x+n+6-2(4-n)}=3^{3x+3n-2}.\]

Multiply powers by adding indices and divide powers by subtracting indices.
steps.title: Solution | Step 2

steps.body:
\[3^{3x+3n-2}=3^x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad3x+3n-2=x.\]

The base-3 exponential is one-to-one, so equal powers have equal indices.
steps.title: Solution | Step 3

steps.body:
\[2x=2-3n\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=1-\frac{3n}{2}.\]

Collect the x terms and divide by 2.
steps.title: Solution | Step 4
